summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with nausea, weakness, and inability to tolerate oral intake one week after a prior discharge for a marginal ulcer following Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. She was dehydrated and started on IV fluids and IV pantoprazole for ulcer protection. On hospital day 3, she developed diarrhea, and stool testing confirmed Clostridium difficile infection. Oral metronidazole was initiated, and Infectious Disease recommended a 14-day course. Sucralfate was added for ulcer coating. Her symptoms resolved over the course of the admission, and she advanced to a stage 3 bariatric diet. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue omeprazole, sucralfate, metronidazole, and crushed oral medications, with follow-up in the surgical clinic.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
